newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM says Berisha ouster would cause vacuum.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM says Berisha ouster would cause vacuum.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino on Saturday dismissed calls for embattled President Sali Berisha to quit, saying his resignation would cause a power vacuum in a country still reeling from weeks of unrest.

In a clear rebuff to rebels in southern Albania who have been demanding that Berisha should resign, Fino said in an interview with Reuters that the government had more pressing tasks in restoring order and distributing humanitarian aid.
Fino, a member of the opposition Socialist Party, was appointed last week by Berisha to lead an interim national unity government ahead of elections in June.
But he has been locked in a power struggle with Berisha's Democrats who control 122 of the 140 seats in parliament after elections last May that international observers said were deeply flawed.
"The government has a more important mission than asking for the president's resignation," Fino said. "It would create an institutional vacuum if Berisha were to resign."

Opposition leaders have made it clear that they want an end to Berisha's presidency, but they would prefer this was brought about by democratic means. Berisha himself has promised to quit if his party loses the June election.
Fino was speaking a day after rebel leaders from 14 towns in southern Albania issued a fresh call for Berisha to resign, but pulled back from a confrontation with the government.

Albania's unrest blew up first in the south after shady pyramid investment schemes collapsed and left thousands of families destitute. Angry Albanians looted thousands of guns from army barracks and took control of their towns.
Fino said he was ready to open a dialogue with the south, but urged the rebels to come up with a coherent consensus that would help the government restore order.
A delegation from the rebel held southern port of Vlore was expected to meet Fino on Saturday.
The prime minister acknowledged that outside aid could not be delivered to Albania in significant quantities until order was restored.

Fino, who travels to Rome for talks next week with European Union foreign ministers, urged the EU and the United States to move more quickly to help Albania, which he said was a member of the "big European family".

"Europe and the United States have given their message and I thank them for their strong support of the government of national reconciliation," Fino said. "But I would like them to move faster in providing concrete economic assistance."
Italy said on Friday it was preparing to send emergency health supplies to Albania over the weekend after a request from Fino.

In their statement on Friday, southern rebel leaders demanded that the government investigate the collapsed pyramid schemes with a view to finding ways of repaying people's losses. Albanians are estimated to have sunk up to $2 billion into the schemes.

But Fino made it clear that there was no immediate prospect of the interim national unity government being able to return any lost money and he personally thought it was "impossible that losses would be repaid.
He suggested however that an all-party commission might be set up to examine the problem of the pyramid scheme companies.
